title: Single sign-on
hint: Let this system sign users in through your existing identity provider (Okta, Keycloak, Entra ID, and so on). This system is only the relying party; it does not become an identity provider itself.

localAlwaysOn.title: Local accounts always keep working
localAlwaysOn.body: Local username and password sign-in stays available after you turn on single sign-on. When the identity provider is down, misconfigured, or its certificate has expired, that is the only way back in — which is why it cannot be switched off.

field.issuerHint: The provider's base URL. Enter it and press Discover; the remaining endpoints are fetched for you. HTTPS only, and it cannot resolve to a private address.
field.secretHint: Write-only. No endpoint ever reads it back.
field.redirectHint: Register this line verbatim in the provider's application. One wrong character and sign-in fails with redirect_uri_mismatch, which reports neither the expected nor the actual value.
field.scopesHint: Must include openid, otherwise the provider returns no id_token and sign-in stops at the last step.
field.usernameClaimHint: Which claim in the id_token to use as the username. Providers differ widely: Okta usually has preferred_username, others use sub or email. If it is wrong, the sign-in error lists the claims the provider actually sent.
field.jit: Create an account automatically when someone from the provider signs in for the first time
field.jitRoleHint: This sets their ceiling. When unsure, leave it read-only — granting more later is easier than taking it back.
field.allowPrivateHint: Tick this when the provider is on a private network or reachable only over HTTP. It is off by default to block one specific risk: this probe is sent by the server, so without a limit anyone could point it at an internal address and use it to scan the network. Self-hosted Keycloak or AD FS is a normal case — just tick it.

jit.seatsBody: Once enabled, anyone in the identity provider consumes a seat by signing in once, with no approval step. Exceeding your licensed seats does not block sign-in, but it is logged — and it is usually discovered at renewal. If your headcount is manageable, leave this off and create accounts by hand.

error.title: Cannot load the single sign-on configuration

reason.sso_disabled: Single sign-on is not enabled. Use a local account, or ask an administrator to turn it on.
reason.idp_unreachable: Cannot reach the identity provider. This is usually outbound network access or an allowlist on their side, not a problem with your account.
reason.state_invalid: This sign-in attempt has expired or was already used. Start again — waiting too long invalidates it.
reason.missing_code: The identity provider returned no authorization code. Please sign in again.
reason.idp_returned_error: The identity provider rejected this sign-in. If you cancelled the prompt, just try again; otherwise ask an administrator to check the application settings.
reason.code_exchange_failed: Exchanging the authorization code failed. Usually the client secret or redirect URI does not match what is registered with the provider; an administrator needs to check.
reason.id_token_invalid: The token from the identity provider failed verification and sign-in was refused. This is a security check; please contact an administrator.
reason.no_subject: The token from the identity provider carries no user identifier, so you cannot be identified.
reason.username_claim_missing: No username available: the configured claim is not present in what the provider returned. An administrator needs to change "Username comes from".
reason.user_resolve_failed: Your identity was verified, but you have no account here and automatic account creation is off. Ask an administrator to create one.
reason.session_failed: Your identity was verified, but the session could not be created. Try again, and contact an administrator if it keeps failing.
reason.state_save_failed: Could not start sign-in — the server failed to store this attempt. Please try again.
reason.unknown: Sign-in did not complete and no reason was reported. Try again or use a local account.

lastError.title: Most recent sign-in failure
lastError.claimsHint: Set "Username comes from" above to one of these. This list comes from a real sign-in attempt, so it beats the documentation.
lastError.cleared: This clears itself after the next successful sign-in.

redirectMismatch.title: The scheme in this callback URL is wrong — registering it as-is will break login
redirectMismatch.body: This page is served over {{page}}, but the URL above was computed as {{uri}}. The usual cause is a gateway terminating TLS without forwarding the X-Forwarded-Proto header, so the backend inferred the wrong scheme. Register this instead:
redirectMismatch.fix: Register the corrected line above with your identity provider, and have ops add X-Forwarded-Proto on the reverse proxy — otherwise it will be recomputed wrong every time.
